sentences.span: only a 68% market probability the FOMC hikes at the upcoming meeting, even though Warsh's speech says he tightens
sentences.why: Multiple sources (TS Lombard's 'oddly low probability of a hike' framing, Duttenhoefer's down-day recap on Iran/inflation/yields) support a genuinely undecided, high-stakes Fed-meeting setup; this is a fair composite scene-setter, not a checkable figure.

sentences.span: Treasury yield reached its highest level since October 2023
sentences.why: The 10yr level itself (SPY/QQQ intraday, 4.79-4.80% yield) is unsupported live-market data, but the sentence also asserts Tuesday's move was the highest 'since January 2025' — the only source discussing the milestone says 'since October 2023,' a contradicted date/figure.

sentences.span: Vol-control equity allocations at a maxed out 100th percentile.
sentences.why: Systematic/trend-following funds being maximally long is well supported (TME piece, Goldman/BofA/DB positioning charts). No source anywhere in the set mentions hedge fund equity exposure; the 'hedge funds under-owned' half of the contrast is invented and grafted onto the real systematic-positioning claim.

sentences.span: only a 68% market probability the FOMC hikes at the upcoming meeting
sentences.why: A 66-68% probability is not 'the bond market has decided' anything — TS Lombard explicitly frames it as an 'oddly low probability... 15 days from meeting.' Separately, the DB Reid piece shows long-dated yields breaking to multi-year highs in five countries that day (US, UK, Germany, France, Japan), not three.

sentences.span: markets now pricing 66% probability of a Fed rate hike in Sep
sentences.why: The 66% figure is genuinely from a Goldman note. But no Goldman document in the set argues for a hold — that argument ('he will be poring through the upcoming data to find some wiggle room to hold rates constant... I still think he finds it') is TS Lombard's own view in 15098, misattributed to Goldman.
No document in the source set contains a 2027 cloud-capex forecast of $1.2-1.5trn, an $800bn current-year figure, or language about demand broadening into 'ordinary companies and governments.'

sentences.span: we do not expect Tech/AI to drive returns in 2H… Tech earnings and cash flow are diverging
sentences.why: JPM's thesis that Mag-7 earnings and free cash flow are diverging is real, but the source doesn't say cash flow is negative or that profits are at a 'record' — that specificity is invented and paired with the fabricated dollar figures in s8.
No source gives cloud-builder Q2 capex of $165bn or free cash flow falling from $60bn to $7bn; these numbers do not appear anywhere in the corpus.

No source mentions a software-sector 6.7% rally, Salesforce/CrowdStrike/Okta results, or a Goldman desk position in IGV calls; none of the three Goldman documents in the set reference IGV or software at all.
Opinion resting entirely on the fabricated software/IGV claim in s9, which has no source; the stance itself appears in no document.

There is no Bank of America document anywhere in the day's source set, and no source reports gold up ~10% in August or a $7.3bn weekly gold-fund inflow. The cited attribution doesn't correspond to any ingested document.
None of the three Goldman documents (US Daily Download, Duttenhoefer's Daily, Privorotsky) mention a derivatives desk position buying upside/selling downside on a debasement thesis.
No Goldman document discusses a materials desk view, a broken 100-day moving average, or Chinese selling in materials.

Commentary built entirely on the fabricated diesel-margin revision in s14; no source supports the underlying data point it interprets.
